A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CostBench research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including the image-only annotation screenshot.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of ten LLMs, including static results in Table 4, dynamic-blocking experiments, sensitivity analyses and human validation.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and additionally reports tool-call averages, bootstrap uncertainty estimates and further length-eight results.

M1.justification: The tool construction, cost assignment, agent interaction, blocking mechanisms and trajectory algorithms are retained. The tie-breaking explanation in v2 Appendix B.2 documents a fewer-calls preference already present in v1's inference prompt.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six travel tasks, static sequence lengths five through eight, and four dynamic-blocking types. The new length-eight table expands reporting of existing coverage; Appendix E's other domains are proposed applications, not evaluated additions.

E2.justification: v2 Table 9 adds Greedy Policy to the reported length-eight comparison, whereas v1 Figure 2 compares only the five selected LLMs there. The ten-model main comparison is unchanged, and Claude-Sonnet-4.0 becoming Claude-Sonnet-4 is a naming edit.

E3.justification: v2 introduces average valid tool-call count as an auxiliary measure in Table 6. Its example inference prompt also changes the stated refinement count from one to two dimensions, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Principal settings and the computation underlying UIHR, renamed TCR, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a test-set-resampling analysis addressing whether model differences could reflect sampling noise. Existing task-length, cost-noise, blocking-frequency, seed-sensitivity and error analyses are retained; the three-seed experiment is not new.

E5.justification: v1 reports seed sensitivity but no confidence intervals. v2 Appendix C.2 and Table 8 introduce 10,000 bootstrap resamples of the 381-instance test set and 95% interval half-widths for EMR, ANED and AED across all ten models. The reported additional seeds remain 1000, 2000 and 3000.

E6.justification: The main numerical results and existing plots are unchanged. v2 Table 9 adds length-eight cost-gap, AED, completion and invalid-call results beyond the previously plotted EMR/ANED, plus greedy results including 3.41% EMR. Table 6 adds valid-call averages, such as 2.69 for GPT-5.

T1.justification: The formal tool graph, trajectory definitions, metric equations and n−2 blocking-solvability proof remain unchanged. The worked metric example and discussion of expected costs explain existing mathematics; the bootstrap subsection titled 'Theoretical Bounds' supplies statistical estimates rather than new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the approximately 40% dynamic-performance decline with an unspecified significant decline, reducing the claim's quantitative specificity. The benchmark contributions and central claims about planning weaknesses remain, including the numerical framing elsewhere in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretations of benchmark validity and applicability through blocking-fairness and memorization arguments in B.6.3–B.6.5 and cross-domain generalization arguments in new Appendix E. C.1–C.2 additionally interpret near-greedy Qwen performance as effectively random guessing and confidence intervals as establishing significant model differences. The main travel-domain and simulation limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents ground-truth tie handling and fresh evaluation contexts without cross-instance memory. Tool-library totals are revised to include the factor of six domains. These expand or correct documentation without establishing changes to the underlying library; principal hyperparameters and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on contamination, bootstrap uncertainty, tool-integrated reasoning and budget-aware agent scaling, particularly in the new discussion. It removes the multimodal future-work citation and two scalability citations. Section 2 and Table 1 retain the original comparative positioning.

P1.justification: v2 polishes language, renames UIHR to TCR, moves the open-source/proprietary comparison into D.4, reorganizes the robustness material and inserts a discussion appendix before data annotation. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the metric illustration in Figure 8 and Tables 6, 8 and 9 for call counts, uncertainty and length-eight results. The tool-statistics table moves into the appendix, and headings and captions are adjusted. Existing plots and the overall visual format are preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the evaluation easier to assess through bootstrap uncertainty estimates, additional length-eight results and a worked metric example while preserving the main evidence. These useful gains are tempered by interpretive overreach: Appendix C.2's broad significance claim is not established by the reported marginal confidence intervals alone.
